summary.headline: PCBL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 17% to INR2,474 crore, EBITDA up 23% to INR400 crore, PAT up 65% to INR155 crore, helped by low-cost inventory gains.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 17% YoY to INR2,474 crore and EBITDA rose 23% to INR400 crore, with PAT up 65% to INR155 crore. Management attributed part of the margin to spot-market pricing during the crude spike (Brent averaged USD 97/bbl vs USD 78 in Q4 FY26) and to low-cost inventory, which it said will partly reverse. Carbon black volumes were flat at 153,513 tonnes as export volumes were diverted to higher-margin domestic spot, and management guided Q2 volumes lower on customer destocking before a recovery in H2. Aquapharm (new CEO Rohit Narang) delivered revenue of INR394 crore and EBITDA of INR47 crore, with oil and gas weak YoY.

financial_highlights.change: reduced as volume diverted to domestic spot
INR40-50 crore expected to reverse next quarter

segments.name: Carbon black - Tyres
segments.commentary: Tyre segment volume 91,379 MT in Q1. Management cites Indian tyre industry growth of 7-8% in FY26 and high single-digit growth expected FY27-29.

segments.name: Carbon black - Performance chemicals
segments.commentary: Volume 42,386 MT in Q1, down sequentially; export margins lower due to freight, so volume was pushed to domestic market.

segments.name: Specialty carbon black
segments.commentary: Volume 19,748 MT, up 23% YoY; around 70% sold internationally. 20,000 MTPA Mundra specialty line commissioned in Q1 FY27, taking total installed carbon black capacity to 900,000 MTPA.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Generation 217 million units; external sales 130 million units at improved realisation, which drove the EBIT rise to about INR110 crore from about INR80 crore.

segments.name: Aquapharm
segments.commentary: Revenue INR394 crore, EBITDA INR47 crore. Application-specific solutions volume +10% YoY; oil and gas down 35% YoY but up 50% QoQ; home care and water solutions volume down marginally YoY. Q1 EBITDA/tonne about INR20,000 vs about INR19,500 in the same quarter last year.

guidance_outlook: Carbon black FY27 EBITDA per tonne guided at 14-15% above FY26 average, i.e. about INR16,500-17,000/MT; reiterated on the call.
Management modelling anchor for remaining nine months: about INR36-38/MT gross profit/EBITDA per tonne, subject to volume-margin trade-off.
Q2 FY27 volumes expected to be affected by customer destocking and cautious procurement; management views this as timing, not demand, and expects volume growth in Q3 and Q4.
Cost efficiency programme targets INR200-250 crore savings over the next 4-6 quarters; management says the target holds.
FY27 capex about INR300 crore (plus or minus INR50 crore), largely efficiency/maintenance; strategic capex about INR100 crore; Andhra greenfield spend shifts mainly to FY28.

Aquapharm: no raw-material surcharge assumed for the rest of FY27; management expects a better FY27 number led by volume. Exit run-rate guidance of INR75 crore EBITDA not reaffirmed; new CEO says it is too early.
Tariff refund from US of about INR40-45 crore (Aquapharm and PCBL combined) expected in 2-4 weeks; accounting treatment to be confirmed with auditors.
Nanovace pilot plant: sampling to start in August; first batch to customers in the next few weeks.
capex_capacity: Total installed carbon black capacity now 900,000 MTPA after commissioning of 20,000 MTPA specialty line at Mundra in Q1 FY27.
Chennai rubber-grade capacity commissioned; management says the added capacity supports rubber-grade volume.
Nanovace silicon anode pilot plant at Palej: consent to operate received for R&D and sampling; machine-level trials started.
1,000 MTPA super-conductive specialty black facility set up at Palej; market development started.
Acetylene black: first-phase modular plant engineering complete; product development under way with technology collaborator.
Coal tar distillation project under definition; capex approvals expected within about one month.
Aquapharm: new green chelates facility under discussion as current capacity is oversubscribed.
demand_pricing: Brent averaged USD 97/bbl in Q1 vs USD 78 in Q4 FY26; spot volumes (about one-third of total) captured higher realisations as crude rose in April-May.
Average realisation rose about INR27,000/MT QoQ, of which about INR11,000-12,000/MT was margin from better spot pricing and the rest was cost pass-through (per CFO).
CBFS-CBO spread stated at about USD 150/tonne, with CBO higher; management says the relationship holds.
Europe carbon black volume about 16,000 MT and US about 4,800 MT in Q1.
Logistics: inbound and outbound freight remain high and erratic; some surcharges recovered but not fully.
US customers diversifying away from China and Russia; management says PCBL is more competitive in the US than pre-conflict despite higher freight.
Aquapharm: phosphonates growing in Asia; Europe shifting to green chelates; oil and gas demand volatile with customer inventory overhang in the Americas.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the quarter's profit came from low-cost inventory gains, and how much of the performance chemicals volume dip is export-linked?
qa_highlights.answer: Low-cost inventory benefit was about INR70 crore in Q1, of which INR40-50 crore may reverse next quarter. Performance chemicals volume was diverted to domestic market because export margins were lower on higher freight; specialty is about 70% international and was not hit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tariff refund amount and where will it be booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined refund for Aquapharm and PCBL is about INR40-45 crore; application is filed and receipt expected in 2-4 weeks. Accounting treatment (top line vs other income) to be confirmed with auditors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable Aquapharm EBITDA per tonne and full-year run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 EBITDA/tonne about INR20,000 vs about INR19,500 a year ago. Next quarter may be lower due to inventory adjustment; management expects full-year EBITDA/tonne to be sustainable at similar levels. Utilisation remains low.

qa_highlights.question: Why did carbon black volumes fall QoQ and YoY despite the Chennai line, and what is the gross profit per kg trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it chose not to deliver some international orders where logistics ate margins, and held low-cost inventory for sale when new prices came in. Destocking in Q2; volume recovery expected in Q3 and Q4. Gross profit per tonne targeted at about INR36-38 for the remaining nine months, a trade-off with volume.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q1 carbon black EBITDA per tonne, FY27 guidance and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 carbon black EBITDA was about INR22,900/MT. FY27 guidance of 14-15% above FY26 average, about INR16,500-17,000/MT, reiterated. FY27 capex about INR300 crore (plus or minus INR50 crore), with strategic capex up to about INR100 crore; Andhra greenfield spend mainly in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Nanovace and the long-term INR1,000 crore EBITDA ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilot plant is up, with machine-level trials done and line balancing ongoing; first batch to customers expected in the next few weeks, with sampling in August. Management reiterated that Nanovace will hit its targets, without restating timelines or the INR1,000 crore figure.

risks_watch: Inventory-gain reversal: about INR40-50 crore expected to reverse in Q2, and management flagged that Q1 margins are unlikely to repeat.
Q2 FY27 carbon black volumes: customer destocking and cautious procurement; recovery depends on volume growth in Q3 and Q4.
Freight and logistics: inbound and outbound costs remain high and erratic; surcharges recovered only partially, and some ports are temporarily out of action.
Aquapharm: oil and gas volatility with inventory overhang in the Americas; exit run-rate of INR75 crore EBITDA not reaffirmed by the new CEO; raw material availability and LPG constraints.
Spot-price exposure: about one-third of volumes on spot, with part of the margin tied to crude moves that may moderate.
Cost programme: INR200-250 crore savings over 4-6 quarters, with delivery in reported results still to be shown; coal tar distillation capex approvals expected within about a month.
key_quotes: Close to a third of our volumes are on the spot market, and our teams monetize this exposure very effectively as crude ran up sharply through April and May, capturing strong realizations.
We see this as a timing effect, not a demand effect and therefore, remain constructive on the second half of FY27.
This quarter we have some extraordinary benefit of low-cost inventory, which is unlikely to be repeated in subsequent quarters.
So Nanovace, we continue to hold that it will hit the targets that we had set ourselves.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on structural tailwinds (trade deals, US tariff advantage, Russian supply contraction) and on the battery materials pipeline. Cautious on near-term volumes and on the sustainability of Q1 margins, with several answers pointing to inventory and spot effects that will reverse. Evasive on Aquapharm's INR75 crore exit run-rate, which the new CEO said is too early to reaffirm.

1,000 MTPA super-conductive specialty black facility at Palej (set up; market development started)
Acetylene black first-phase modular plant (engineering complete; product development under way)
Coal tar distillation project (under definition; capex approvals expected within about one month)
Andhra greenfield carbon black plant (spend shifts mainly to FY28)

growth.why: Q1 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR2,474 crore, but Q1 margins were lifted by one-off spot pricing and ~INR70 crore low-cost inventory gains that partly reverse; management guides good FY27 volume growth and FY27 carbon black EBITDA/t of INR16,500-17,000 with Q2 volumes soft on destocking, while the 20,000 MTPA Mundra line added ~2.3% to capacity.
